title.en: History: Evolution of Humans and Society - Prehistoric Period

text.en: Asha found a stone tool in a museum. "Who made this?" she asked.

History is the study of the human past. The Prehistoric period, before writing, is divided into the Stone Age (Palaeolithic, Mesolithic and Neolithic) and the Metal Age. Early humans were hunter-gatherers who used stone tools and learned to make fire.
In the Neolithic age people began farming and settled in villages, and they made pottery and domesticated animals. Later the Chalcolithic, Bronze and Iron ages brought metal tools. Evidence comes from fossils, tools, cave paintings and burial sites, and sites such as Adichanallur in Tamil Nadu show early life in the south.
Human evolution passed from Australopithecus to Homo habilis, Homo erectus and Homo sapiens. Sources of history are archaeological and literary, and archaeologists study the remains of the past.

problem.en: Why was farming a turning point in history?

text.en: People could grow food in one place.
This led to growth of towns and trade.

prompt.en: A friend says Early humans lived in cities. How will you reply?

points.en: Neolithic means farming and settled life.
